problem: Image editing methods using text-to-image models suffer from accumulated drift when the reconstruction path uses mismatched timesteps, limiting reconstruction fidelity.
approach: DirectEdit eliminates reconstruction error by directly aligning forward paths instead of rectifying the inversion path, using attention feature injection and multi-branch mask-guided noise blending for feature sharing.
contribution: Achieves efficient and accurate image editing with superior performance over state-of-the-art methods without introducing additional neural function evaluations.

problem: Label noise in federated graph learning degrades global model generalization, and existing federated label-noise methods designed for vision tasks yield suboptimal results when applied to graph data.
approach: FedRGL leverages globally aggregated models and local subgraph structure to implement class-aware dual-consistency filtering for noise-node identification, then assigns pseudo-labels using graph contrastive learning augmentations.
contribution: Achieves 5-8% higher accuracy on average and up to 30% improvement over weaker baselines under various noise conditions across real-world graph datasets.

problem: Translating natural-language descriptions of decision problems into formal optimization code is brittle with large language models, often generating syntactically invalid or non-executable code.
approach: NEMO uses autonomous coding agents with sandboxed execution to guarantee code validity by construction, employing asymmetric validation loops, external memory for experience reuse, and minimum Bayes risk decoding.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on nine optimization benchmarks with substantial margins on several datasets by treating autonomous coding agents as first-class abstractions.

problem: DiLoCo's outer synchronization is bandwidth-heavy and brittle to stragglers and transient failures in low-bandwidth distributed training settings.
approach: Factored Gossip DiLoCo replaces exact synchronization with approximate gossip-based mixing, factorizing synchronization into non-blocking mixing overlapped with computation and blocking tightening steps.
contribution: Substantially improves compute utilization on billion-parameter language models in low-bandwidth settings with training progress ranging from comparable to closely matching standard DiLoCo.

problem: Retrieval-augmented generation for multimodal document QA breaks document structure and cross-modal alignment, and iterative retrieval fails by looping on partial evidence without persistent global search state.
approach: G²-Reader maintains a Content Graph preserving document structure and cross-modal semantics, plus a Planning Graph of sub-questions to track findings and guide stepwise navigation for evidence completion.
contribution: Reaches 66.21% average accuracy on VisDoMBench, outperforming strong baselines and standalone GPT-5 at 53.08% with Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct.

problem: Uniform computation budgets in LLM decoding over-compute on easy tokens and under-compute on hard ones, wasting inference resources since token difficulty varies widely.
approach: Self-Optimizing Language Models pair a frozen LLM with a lightweight policy network that selects discrete efficiency actions per token, controlling attention sparsity, MLP pruning, and activation quantization bit-width.
contribution: Improves quality at matched budget over static allocation and strong random schedule search, offering a complementary axis for inference-efficiency optimization.

problem: Model merging on Mixture-of-Experts architectures fails due to routing breakdown, where the merged router cannot dispatch tokens to suitable experts after parameter perturbations.
approach: Hessian-Aware Router Calibration leverages second-order curvature information to realign the merged router using a closed-form solution solvable via matrix-free conjugate gradient.
contribution: Effectively mitigates routing breakdown across diverse MoE merging baselines with substantial performance improvements on mathematical reasoning and code generation tasks.

problem: No single action space is universally best for building generalist AI agents; effective action spaces are highly task-dependent, complicating the goal of one agent for all tasks.
approach: Chain-of-Action unifies high-level abstract and low-level control actions in a single model, using abstract goals as intermediate reasoning steps that guide precise executable action generation.
contribution: OpenHA achieves state-of-the-art performance as an All-in-One generalist agent trained on diverse action spaces, outperforming strong specialized baselines on over 800 Minecraft tasks.

problem: Bayesian experimental design cannot handle both partially observable dynamical systems and fully online inference, where latent states make likelihood and information-theoretic objectives intractable.
approach: Derives new estimators of expected information gain and gradients that marginalize latent states via nested particle filters, enabling scalable stochastic optimization in nonlinear state-space models.
contribution: Successfully handles partial observability and online inference on realistic models like SIR and moving source location tasks with convergence guarantees.

problem: Existing RL backdoor attacks rely on unrealistic white-box access to parameters, rewards, or observations, missing practical black-box supply-chain vulnerabilities.
approach: Supply-Chain Backdoor attack poisons the dataset through legitimate agent-environment interactions by training with third-party policies in a black-box manner.
contribution: Demonstrates over 90% peak attack success rate and reduces victim returns by 80% with only 3% data corruption, exposing critical vulnerabilities in the RL supply chain.

problem: Long-form video understanding in VLMs faces tension between computational constraints and capturing information across thousands of frames without reliable recovery from poor sampling choices.
approach: VideoBrain uses dual complementary agents—CLIP-based semantic retrieval and Uniform temporal sampling—with behavior-aware rewards teaching when agent invocation is genuinely beneficial.
contribution: Achieves 3.5-9.0% improvement over baseline while using 30-40% fewer frames with strong cross-dataset generalization to short videos.

problem: Decoupled offline speculator training introduces high time-to-serve lag, delayed utility feedback, and domain-drift degradation as target models are repurposed to new domains.
approach: Aurora reframes online speculator learning as asynchronous reinforcement learning from live inference traces, using accepted tokens for positive feedback and rejected proposals for implicit negative feedback.
contribution: Supports day-0 deployment with immediate utility feedback and rapid domain adaptation while continuously improving system performance from live traffic.

problem: Q-based imitation learning methods like IQ-Learn claim to outperform behavioral cloning but actually reduce to BC, remaining susceptible to compounding errors under partial observability.
approach: Dual Q-DM uses Bellman constraints to drive value flow—Q-values propagate from demonstrated to unvisited states via environment dynamics—enabling generalization beyond demonstrations.
contribution: First non-adversarial imitation learning method theoretically guaranteed to eliminate compounding errors, equivalent to adversarial imitation learning in mitigating horizon-dependent gaps.

problem: Budget-feasible procurement mechanism design focuses on buyer value maximization, neglecting buyer utility (value minus payments) and welfare (value minus costs) objectives.
approach: Designs simple mechanisms achieving constant-factor approximation for welfare in prior-free settings and near-optimal utility in Bayesian settings with ex-post budget constraints.
contribution: Introduces mechanisms for utility-optimal and welfare-optimal procurement beyond value-maximization, with generalizations to other objectives.

problem: Text-to-CAD systems hallucinate missing dimensions and follow inconsistent instructions when geometric descriptions are under-specified or internally contradictory.
approach: ProCAD pairs a proactive clarifying agent auditing prompts and asking targeted questions with a CAD coding agent, enabling self-consistent specification before synthesis.
contribution: Reduces mean Chamfer distance by 79.9% and lowers invalidity ratio from 4.8% to 0.9%, outperforming Claude Sonnet 4.5 with low interaction overhead.

problem: Diffusion models produce semantic inconsistencies (hallucinations) and existing guidance methods add computational overhead or require external signals and architectural modifications.
approach: TAG amplifies tangential score components using an intermediate sample as projection basis, steering toward higher-probability regions without extra training or architecture changes.
contribution: Corrects sampling trajectory with negligible overhead, reducing inconsistencies and improving fidelity as a training-free, architecture-agnostic plug-and-play guidance method.

problem: RL for open-ended tasks with vast solution spaces lacks objective ground truth, and pointwise reward scoring induces discrimination collapse where reward models fail to distinguish subtle advantages.
approach: ArenaRL shifts from pointwise scoring to intra-group relative ranking via process-aware pairwise evaluation, constructing adversarial arenas with tournament-based ranking for stable advantage signals.
contribution: Achieves O(N) complexity with high-precision advantage estimation, introducing two benchmarks (Open-Travel, Open-DeepResearch) for open-ended agent training and evaluation.

problem: Reasoning models handle symbol symmetries only implicitly via expensive data augmentation, failing to exploit permutation invariances architecturally.
approach: SE-RRMs enforce permutation equivariance at the architectural level through symbol-equivariant layers, guaranteeing identical solutions under symbol or color permutations.
contribution: Outperforms prior RRMs on 9×9 Sudoku and generalizes from training data to smaller (4×4) and larger (16×16, 25×25) instances with only 2M parameters.

problem: Scene-centric benchmarks evaluate unconstrained environments where single images admit multiple plausible 3D interpretations, failing to test spatial reasoning in determinate settings.
approach: SSI-Bench uses structural constraints from geometry, topology, and physical feasibility to make 3D relations determinate, containing 1,000 ranking questions requiring full 3D relation resolution.
contribution: Reveals large human-model gap: best open-source model 22.2%, strongest closed-source 33.6%, humans 91.6%, showing fundamental spatial-understanding limitations with minimal gains from chain-of-thought.

problem: Adversaries can inject malicious records into LLM-agent memory to bias behavior, but effective injections are visibly malicious while stealthy injections are less effective.
approach: MemIncept generates cooperative query sets via bidirectional evolutionary strategy: forward pass ensures collective target outcome, backward pass ensures semantic closeness to benign queries.
contribution: Achieves high success rates comparable to explicit attacks while remaining difficult to flag under automated filters, demonstrating practical memory-poisoning vulnerabilities.

problem: Tubal Nuclear Norm applies uniform penalties to frequency-domain singular values without distinguishing inter-frequency sparsity from intra-frequency low-rankness, limiting flexibility for multi-level spectral structures.
approach: Tensor ℓp-Schatten-q quasi-norm enables explicit control of dual spectral sparsity by jointly regularizing inter-frequency sparsity and intra-frequency low-rankness with theoretical minimax error bounds.
contribution: Subsumes TNN as special case with reweighted optimization for nonconvex problems, demonstrating effectiveness and robustness on tensor completion and image clustering.

problem: Non-generative vision models fail to achieve compositional generalization that is hallmark of human data efficiency, yet generative approaches require complex inductive biases.
approach: Formalizes that encoder-based (non-generative) methods require substantially more complex inductive biases than decoder-based (generative) methods for compositional generalization.
contribution: Demonstrates theoretically that generative methods with simple decoder biases outperform non-generative methods requiring large-scale pretraining for compositional generalization.

problem: Existing LLM unlearning methods based on prediction loss maximization face issues of over-forgetting and poor model utility.
approach: DareU uses reinforcement learning to reduce data attribution scores of generated responses to forget-data owners, shifting optimization target from loss maximization to de-attribution.
contribution: Outperforms existing baseline approaches, achieving effective unlearning while balancing forget quality and model utility through attribution rewards.

problem: Robotic manipulation of flat objects is challenging due to ungraspable configurations, strong geometry/material variations, and limited generalization in closed-setting evaluations.
approach: Decouples manipulation into strategy generator predicting object-invariant strategies from point clouds via contrastive learning, and execution module decomposing into reusable action primitives.
contribution: Introduces FlatLab benchmark with high-fidelity simulation and standardized protocols; demonstrates effective generalization to unseen objects and categories.

problem: Most deep research frameworks rely on rigid one-shot workflows with long autonomous runs, offering little room for course correction when user intent shifts.
approach: SteER introduces mid-process interpretable control using cost-benefit formulation to pause when beneficial, combines diversity-aware planning with utility signals rewarding alignment/novelty/coverage.
contribution: Outperforms baselines by up to 22.80% on alignment, leads on quality metrics, and is preferred by humans in 85%+ pairwise judgments.

problem: Verbalized confidence in LLMs fails to calibrate universally across diverse tasks without degrading accuracy.
approach: Decomposes confidence into reasoning uncertainty and evidence localization uncertainty, enabling task-aware semantics that restore cross-family generalization via supervised fine-tuning.
contribution: Shows universal confidence calibration fails across task families but within-family transfer works; decompositional approach restores cross-family generalization.

problem: Surrogate models for topology optimization exhibit highly variable out-of-distribution generalization under distribution shifts like changing loads or boundary conditions.
approach: Introduces pseudo-sensitivities to characterize which physical fields enable generalization, conditioning Bernoulli flow-matching generators on sensitivity-equivalent fields for information-theoretic optimality.
contribution: Sensitivity-conditioned matching yields state-of-the-art out-of-distribution performance across structural and CFD topology optimization under load and boundary-condition shifts.

problem: Cloud-edge collaborative speculative decoding suffers from sequential token generation/communication with low resource utilization and inflexible verification triggering causing premature or costly operations.
approach: PipeSD overlaps token generation and communication via token-batch pipeline scheduling optimized by dynamic programming, with dual-threshold verification and Bayesian optimization autotuning.
contribution: Achieves 1.16-2.16× speedup and reduces energy consumption by 14.3-25.3% across draft-target pairs on real-world cloud-edge testbeds.

problem: Test-time guidance in diffusion-based navigation can produce unreliable trajectories when updates drift off the training manifold.
approach: Fisher Preserving Guidance avoids large Fisher drift via low-rank Jacobian factorization requiring single backward pass, with Truncated Fisher Denoising Sensitivity for uncertainty-based multi-sample blending.
contribution: Demonstrates consistent improvements in navigation performance over diffusion-policy baselines without additional training on Maze2D, PushT, and real robot tasks.

problem: KV cache compression evaluations focus on sparse retrieval tasks, masking degradation in reasoning tasks where chain-of-thought coherence is critical.
approach: ShotKV explicitly separates prefill and decoding phases to prioritize semantic units (few-shot examples), preserving chain-of-thought links while enabling aggressive compression.
contribution: Achieves 9-18% accuracy improvements on long-context generation tasks while delivering 11% latency reduction compared to full cache inference.

problem: Standard point-wise residual minimization in Physics-Informed Neural Networks suffers from convergence pathologies in topologically complex domains like TPMS due to locality bias.
approach: MUSA-PINN reformulates Navier-Stokes constraints as integral conservation laws over hierarchical spherical control volumes with flux-balance residuals and skeleton-aware meso-scale volumes.
contribution: Outperforms baselines on steady incompressible flow in TPMS geometries, reducing relative errors by up to 93% while preserving mass conservation.

problem: Attention scores diminish in long contexts, raising questions about token distinguishability and whether it can be preserved.
approach: Introduces Aitchison distance to quantify relative differences among attention probabilities, showing that token distinguishability converges to non-zero limit with Gaussian queries/keys.
contribution: Derives theoretical lower bound of Ω(√log L) on temperature scaling for sharp attention, providing principled alternative to entropy for monitoring training.

problem: Grounded visual reasoning methods impose high computational costs via multi-round ground-then-answer processes while requiring accurate region selection.
approach: RTAF feeds low-resolution thumbnails for reasoning about relevant regions and high-resolution crops for answering, with tool access for extreme cases and reinforcement learning training.
contribution: Based on Qwen2.5-VL, achieves 5.8 point performance gain with comparable or reduced computation through thumbnail reasoning and focused answering.

problem: Multi-view clustering with missing views and cross-view sample misalignment causes inferior clustering performance and hinders cross-view modeling.
approach: OPTION uses conditional flow matching for manifold-preserving missing-view imputation and Gromov-Wasserstein structural regularization for alignment-free fusion in latent space.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art methods across ideal, incomplete, and unaligned scenarios with optional contrastive regularization for aligned settings.

problem: Prompt sensitivity causes unpredictable LLM performance variations between instruction-based and example-based prompting styles.
approach: Identifies task-specific attention heads whose outputs describe the task (lexical task heads) that are shared across prompting styles and trigger answer production.
contribution: Shows behavioral variation can be explained by activation degree of lexical heads, with failures sometimes due to competing task representations diluting target signals.

problem: Multi-modal Diffusion Language Models suffer from visual hallucinations due to static visual perception without sequential dependencies to dynamically interact with visual content.
approach: VGR detects hallucinated spans via confidence fluctuation during denoising and corrects them through targeted visual evidence extraction and in-place remasking.
contribution: Reduces hallucinations and recalls more details on image captioning and hallucination evaluation benchmarks by exploiting diffusion dynamics.

problem: Two-stage agent heterogeneity in intervention policy learning creates distinct agent types with varying returns, but existing methods fail to fully identify all types.
approach: Proposes minimax approach within counterfactual principal strata framework with three estimators (P-OR, P-IPS, P-DR) providing unbiasedness and robustness guarantees.
contribution: Provides theoretical guarantees for optimal intervention allocation accounting for two-stage outcomes with experimental validation of effectiveness.

problem: Reasoning models become confident in answers early but continue generating tokens without revealing internal beliefs, conflating performative with genuine reasoning.
approach: Compares activation probing, early forced answering, and CoT monitors across models, finding models' final answers are decodable from activations earlier than monitors report.
contribution: Probe-guided early exit reduces tokens by up to 80% on MMLU and 30% on GPQA-Diamond with similar accuracy, enabling detection of performative reasoning.

problem: Multi-vector retrieval systems like ColBERT provide superior quality but incur significantly increased search latency compared to single-vector approaches.
approach: LEMUR reduces multi-vector similarity search to supervised learning solved by one-hidden-layer neural network, then reduces inference to single-vector search in latent space.
contribution: Order of magnitude faster than prior multi-vector similarity search methods while maintaining quality advantages.

problem: Manifold clustering methods focus on combining K-means with manifold learning but overlook consistency between data structures and labels, suffering from high computational cost.
approach: LMBC uses label information to guide manifold construction ensuring consistency, introduces anchor-induced distance representation for compact manifold modeling, and maximizes Schatten-p norm for class balance.
contribution: Demonstrates effectiveness and scalability on benchmark datasets with theoretical analysis supporting balance maintenance.
